questions.question: The body lists three conditions — at least one of which must hold to justify multi-agent. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
options: Context explosion: a single loop's window cannot hold all intermediate artifacts
Specialization: retrieval, computation, and writing each need dedicated tools and prompts
Parallel speed: independent subtasks run concurrently, wall-clock time divided by worker count
A cheaper model: using a smaller model is more cost-effective
questions.explanation: See the "When multi-agent is actually justified" section: the three conditions are context explosion, specialization, and parallel speed; if none of the three apply, stick with single-agent. "A cheaper model" is not a listed justification.

questions.question: The "risk" side of context isolation among workers shows up as what?
options: Each worker's window only holds its own task, so prompts can be extremely specialised
Workers cannot see the global picture — they do not know what other workers are doing, so outputs may overlap or even contradict
The orchestrator must bill each worker separately
questions.explanation: See the "Context isolation: feature and risk" section: as a risk, workers cannot see the global picture — they do not know what other workers are doing, so their outputs may overlap with or contradict other workers; stitching and fallback are always the orchestrator's job.

questions.question: After the orchestrator receives a failure report from a worker, which of the following is NOT a handling option the body lists?
options: Redeploy that worker (if time and budget allow)
Reassign the task to another worker that already has related context (low marginal cost)
Degrade gracefully (explicitly flagging the missing data or switching to secondary sources)
Let the worker retry in place indefinitely until it succeeds
questions.explanation: See the "Failure propagation and responsibility" section: the orchestrator's options after a failure are redeploy, reassign to another worker, or degrade gracefully; "retry in place indefinitely until it succeeds" is not a listed option and runs contrary to T03's failure discipline.
